newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks finish sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: French stocks finish sharply lower.

text.p: French stocks finished sharply lower on Wednesday as investors took profits on the market's gains ahead of the publication of the U.S. Federal Reserve's Beige Book and upcoming U.S. producer price data.
Brokers said the market came under late pressure from weaker bond prices and an early fall on Wall Street. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 44.45 points, or 1.65 percent, at 2,641.
Volume was around nine billion francs.
* BNP falls 5.74 percent to 243 francs on rumours UAP, now part of Axa-UAP, may sell its BNP stake.
* Rhone-Poulenc falls 5.22 percent to 190.50 francs, pressured by Hoechst forecast for lower sales in 1997.
* Lafarge rose 1.22 percent to 372 francs on rise in 1996 operating profit and forecast for higher 1997 profit.
* Cie de Suez falls 4.19 percent to 284.40 francs on reports casting doubt on rumours of a Suez-Lyonnaise linkup.
* Alcatel down 3.13 percent at 620 francs after state barred Aerospatiale from joining its bid for Thomson-CSF. Alcatel said it would bid jointly with Dassault.
